name: k_hop_neighborhood
author: e7c02e9e
description: Finds every node within k steps (hops) of a start node using breadth-first search, and registers them with the start node as a subgraph (result_graph_id) that other tools can analyse. Use for questions like 'who is within two hops of Alice?', 'which airports can I reach in at most 2 flights from Chennai?' or 'show everything near node X'. Works on directed and undirected graphs; weights are ignored. On directed graphs, direction says which edges to follow: out (default), in, or both. Returns the number of nodes at each hop distance and the nearest top_k nodes with their hop distance.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

node.description: Id of the start node, e.g. 'MAA' or 'm1'. Not a name: use lookup_node to find the id from a name.

k.description: Maximum number of hops (steps) from the start node. 1 means direct neighbours only; 0 means the start node alone.

direction.description: Directed graphs only (ignored on undirected graphs): 'out' follows edges leaving a node (who can I reach), 'in' follows edges arriving (who can reach me), 'both' ignores edge direction.

top_k.description: How many of the nearest nodes to list (the subgraph always contains all of them).
